cataract.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review analyzes the most relevant studies on current surgical strategies to treat glaucoma patients with cataracts. RECENT FINDINGS: No clear evidence has confirmed better results with trabeculectomy alone compared with phacotrabeculectomy. Recent studies have reported successful outcomes combining deep sclerectomy and two-site phacoemulsification. The phacoemulsification cataract extraction will not vary the intraocular pressure of patients with previous deep sclerectomy. Mitomycin C proved to be effective in maintaining lower pressure levels with the combined surgery technique; however, 5-fluorouracil did not show any improvement. Minimally invasive cataract surgery reduces surgical trauma, making it possible to obtain better results with combined surgery and previous glaucoma surgery. SUMMARY: The surgical strategy decision must be customized to every patient.

cataract.abstract: The aim of this study is to provide a comprehensive overview of surgical methods used in the emulsification of posterior polar cataracts (PPCs) that have been devised to minimize the risk of posterior capsule rupture (PCR) and its consequences. A Pubmed and Medline search of relevant literature on PPC was done. Only articles relevant to the treatment of PPC were included. The posterior capsule in eyes with PPC are known to have an abnormal adhesion to the polar opacity or a pre-existing weakness of the capsule that predisposes the eye to PCR. To circumvent the consequences of cleaving the abnormal adhesion, a majority of the surgeons use the anterior approach through the limbus, whereas some advocate the posterior approach through the pars plana. cataract.summary: This article reviews some of the advances that have taken place in the surgical techniques for difficult cataracts such as rock-hard, white, and posterior polar cataracts. cataract.abstract: This article reviews some of the advances that have taken place in the surgical techniques for difficult cataracts such as rock-hard, white, and posterior polar cataracts. Fashioning a central space, modified chopping maneuvers, and creation of multiple small fragments have enabled the surgeon to consistently achieve a successful outcome. A judicious combination of chop and separation movement in a step-by-step manner reduce the stress of the procedure and make it safer. Raised intracapsular pressure and poor visibility are dealt with through various innovative techniques. Use of high-viscosity sodium hyaluronate and double capsulorhexis allow the surgeon to achieve capsulorhexis with a high success rate. A controlled and gentle approach to phacoemulsification has proven to be the key factor for success in posterior polar cataracts.

cataract.abstract: The design and use of materials in the nanoscale size range for addressing medical and health-related issues continues to receive increasing interest. Research in nanomedicine spans a multitude of areas, including drug delivery, vaccine development, antibacterial, diagnosis and imaging tools, wearable devices, implants, high-throughput screening platforms, etc. using biological, nonbiological, biomimetic, or hybrid materials. Many of these developments are starting to be translated into viable clinical products. Here, we provide an overview of recent developments in nanomedicine and highlight the current challenges and upcoming opportunities for the field and translation to the clinic.

cataract.abstract: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is an inherited retinal dystrophy caused by the loss of photoreceptors and characterized by retinal pigment deposits visible on fundus examination. Prevalence of non syndromic RP is approximately 1/4,000. The most common form of RP is a rod-cone dystrophy, in which the first symptom is night blindness, followed by the progressive loss in the peripheral visual field in daylight, and eventually leading to blindness after several decades. Some extreme cases may have a rapid evolution over two decades or a slow progression that never leads to blindness. In some cases, the clinical presentation is a cone-rod dystrophy, in which the decrease in visual acuity predominates over the visual field loss. cataract.abstract: Corneal wound healing is a complex process involving cell death, migration, proliferation, differentiation, and extracellular matrix remodeling. Many similarities are observed in the healing processes of corneal epithelial, stromal and endothelial cells, as well as cell-specific differences. Corneal epithelial healing largely depends on limbal stem cells and remodeling of the basement membrane. During stromal healing, keratocytes get transformed to motile and contractile myofibroblasts largely due to activation of transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) system. Endothelial cells heal mostly by migration and spreading, with cell proliferation playing a secondary role. In the last decade, many aspects of wound healing process in different parts of the cornea have been elucidated, and some new therapeutic approaches have emerged. cataract.abstract: Summary Candida parapsilosis is an emerging major human pathogen that has dramatically increased in significance and prevalence over the past 2 decades, such that C. parapsilosis is now one of the leading causes of invasive candidal disease. Individuals at the highest risk for severe infection include neonates and patients in intensive care units. C. parapsilosis infections are especially associated with hyperalimentation solutions, prosthetic devices, and indwelling catheters, as well as the nosocomial spread of disease through the hands of health care workers. Factors involved in disease pathogenesis include the secretion of hydrolytic enzymes, adhesion to prosthetics, and biofilm formation. cataract.abstract: Scedosporium spp. are increasingly recognized as causes of resistant life-threatening infections in immunocompromised patients. Scedosporium spp. also cause a wide spectrum of conditions, including mycetoma, saprobic involvement and colonization of the airways, sinopulmonary infections, extrapulmonary localized infections, and disseminated infections. Invasive scedosporium infections are also associated with central nervous infection following near-drowning accidents. The most common sites of infection are the lungs, sinuses, bones, joints, eyes, and brain. Scedosporium apiospermum and Scedosporium prolificans are the two principal medically important species of this genus. Pseudallescheria boydii, the teleomorph of S. apiospermum, is recognized by the presence of cleistothecia. glaucoma.summary: Ultrasound cycloplasty (UCP) is a minimally invasive, non-incisional glaucoma procedure that has emerged in recent years and is generally associated with few complications. We report a case of a patient with acute angle-closure glaucoma underwent UCP for IOP control. …
glaucoma.abstract: Ultrasound cycloplasty (UCP) is a minimally invasive, non-incisional glaucoma procedure that has emerged in recent years and is generally associated with few complications. We report a case of a patient with acute angle-closure glaucoma underwent UCP for IOP control. She developed iris neovascularization and neurotrophic keratopathy（NK）at postoperative week 6, followed by hypopyon, flattening of the anterior chamber, and thinning of the peripheral cornea at postoperative week 11, 12, and 14, respectively. We concluded that UCP can lead to anterior segment ischemia (ASI) and NK, which manifest as iris neovascularization, painless corneal epithelial defects, peripheral corneal thinning, hypopyon, and flattening of the anterior chamber. Preoperative screening for high-risk factors is essential before performing UCP.

In subsequent analyses, this dataset may reveal the current status of the use of IG, provide insight into how IG is currently being deployed, supply a standard against which practices can compare when examining their own treatment patterns, …
glaucoma.abstract: INTRODUCTION: We aim to describe the development of the Newton Registry which characterizes the frequency and nature of interventional glaucoma (IG) procedures used for treatment in the USA between 2022 and 2025. METHODS: The Newton Registry contains International Classification of Disease Tenth Edition (ICD-10) codes and Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes from encounters with patients with glaucoma and providers in ophthalmology practices in the USA. Each practice provided a window of data 18-36 months in duration that captured all glaucoma patient and procedure encounters of the practice's providers. Robust data cleaning techniques were applied. Analyses were descriptive in nature and included a qualitative description of the dataset and its structure, the types and severity of glaucoma included, the duration of follow-up and lapse rate, and the frequency and nature of therapeu

glaucoma.title: Unsupervised Classification of Wide-Field Swept-Source Optical Coherence Tomography Reveals Patterns Associated With Glaucoma Severity and Progression.
glaucoma.summary: These findings suggest that the structural patterns associated with VF progression differ according to disease stage and progression criteria. Our hybrid unsupervised method offers a clinically interpretable framework that may facilitate real-time structural assessment and personalized glaucoma monitoring.
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: We investigated the structural patterns associated with visual field (VF) progression using a novel unsupervised hybrid clustering approach that combined archetypal analysis (AA) and fuzzy c-means (FCM). METHODS: AA was used to identify the representative structural archetypes (ATs) from 1803 wide-field swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT) scans obtained from 1803 eyes of 1167 patients with glaucoma or suspected glaucoma, resulting in 10 distinct ATs. Subsequently, FCM was used to calculate the decomposition coefficients of each eye. A subset of 372 eyes with at least five reliable 24-2 VF tests was analyzed to evaluate the association between baseline structural patterns and subsequent VF progression. Progression was defined using three criteria: mean deviation slope, Visual Field Index slope, and pointwise linear regression. RESULTS: We observed stage-dependent d

glaucoma.title: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease misdiagnosed as angle closure: Demographic characteristics, clinical presentation, and visual outcomes.
glaucoma.summary: VKH can uncommonly present as angle closure, often mimicking PAC or SACG. Early clinical suspicion, use of posterior segment imaging (optical coherence tomography, B-scan, ultrasound biomicroscopy), and prompt immunosuppressive therapy are essential for optimal management.
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: To describe the clinical presentation, diagnostic delay, management, and visual outcomes of Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada (VKH) disease presenting initially as angle closure. METHODS: This retrospective study reviewed the medical records of patients diagnosed with VKH who initially presented with angle closure between January 2013 and December 2020. Clinical features, intraocular pressure (IOP), imaging, treatment modalities, and final visual outcomes were analyzed. Univariate and multivariate analyses were performed to identify factors influencing final BCVA (best corrected visual acuity). RESULTS: Among 768 VKH patients, 18 patients (36 eyes; 3.94%) presented with angle closure with a mean age of 44.4 years and a female preponderance (89%). Eighteen eyes had primary angle closure (PAC), and 18 eyes had secondary angle closure glaucoma (SACG) at presentation. The mean IOP at final follo

glaucoma.title: Outcomes of phaco-endocyclophotocoagulation in acute on chronic primary angle closure glaucoma.
glaucoma.summary: Phaco-endocyclophotocoagulation is not only effective but also very safe in controlling IOP and reducing topical medications in PACG eyes that present with acute symptoms. Biometric parameters are significantly different in such eyes when compared to PACG controls.
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: To report the outcomes of endocyclophotocoagulation (ECP) combined with phacoemulsification in primary angle closure glaucoma (PACG) eyes presenting with acute symptoms (A-o-C-PACG) and to compare the biometric characteristics of these eyes with PACG controls. METHODS: Retrospective data collection of consecutive PACG subjects presenting with symptoms of acute angle closure between May 2021 and September 2023. Such subjects were compared to severity-of-glaucoma-matched PACG controls. Only those eyes that underwent phaco-ECP were included. The main outcome measure was intraocular pressure (IOP) and a comparison of biometric parameters between cases and controls. The secondary outcome measures were the number of anti-glaucoma medications (AGMs), best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), and complications. RESULTS: Fifteen study eyes and 26 PACG controls were included; the mean age was

glaucoma.title: Gonioscopy-assisted transluminal trabeculotomy versus trabeculectomy with phacoemulsification in primary open angle glaucoma - One-year outcomes.
glaucoma.summary: Phaco-GATT demonstrated comparable intraocular pressure reduction, medication independence, and surgical success rates to phacotrabeculectomy at one year, with minimal complications.
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: To assess the safety and efficacy of gonioscopy-assisted transluminal trabeculotomy (GATT) with phacoemulsification in primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG). METHODS: In this prospective, nonrandomized, comparative study, patients with POAG underwent either phaco-GATT (Group A, n = 75) or phacotrabeculectomy (Group B, n = 77) and were followed up for one year. Changes in intraocular pressure (IOP), antiglaucoma medications (AGMs), complications, and success rates over one year were compared. Success rate was described under two criteria: 1: IOP between 6 and 21 mmHg and a decrease of >20% from the baseline; 2: IOP between 6 and 18 mmHg and a decrease of >25% from the baseline. RESULTS: Mean IOP decreased by 25.1%, from 17.93 ± 4.29 mmHg to 13.00 ± 3.18 mmHg (P < 0.001) in Group A (n = 70) and by 28% from 17.81 ± 4.52 mmHg to 12.16 ± 3.28 mmHg (P < 0.001) in Group B (n = 74) at one

glaucoma.title: [Biological basis and clinical potential of wound healing modulators in glaucoma surgery].
glaucoma.summary: The purpose of this review is to analyze the molecular mechanisms of postoperative fibrosis of the filtering bleb and critically evaluate pharmacological approaches to modulating its key mediators as a basis for developing more effective and safer strategies to prolong the hypotensive effect of trabeculectomy. …
glaucoma.abstract: The purpose of this review is to analyze the molecular mechanisms of postoperative fibrosis of the filtering bleb and critically evaluate pharmacological approaches to modulating its key mediators as a basis for developing more effective and safer strategies to prolong the hypotensive effect of trabeculectomy. This review examines current approaches to the management of reparative processes in open-angle glaucoma surgery aimed at preventing excessive fibrosis of the outflow pathways and prolonging the hypotensive effect. Glaucoma continues to be the leading cause of irreversible blindness, and surgical reduction of intraocular pressure is the most effective treatment when medical therapy is insufficient. However, up to 50% of surgical procedures fail within 5 years because of subconjunctival and episcleral fibrosis. The review considers the key phases and molecular markers of wound heali

glaucoma.title: [Choroidal status in angle-closure glaucoma].
glaucoma.summary: Glaucoma remains one of the leading causes of irreversible blindness worldwide. Primary angle-closure glaucoma (PACG) is characterized by episodic impairment of aqueous humor outflow and increases in intraocular pressure (IOP), leading to glaucomatous optic neuropathy. …
glaucoma.abstract: Glaucoma remains one of the leading causes of irreversible blindness worldwide. Primary angle-closure glaucoma (PACG) is characterized by episodic impairment of aqueous humor outflow and increases in intraocular pressure (IOP), leading to glaucomatous optic neuropathy. Traditionally, in the pathogenesis of PACG the emphasis has been placed on anterior segment anatomy, but in recent years, the role of the posterior segment, including the choroid, has been attracting increasing interest. This review aimed to evaluate, based on the literature, the possible role of choroidal changes in the pathogenesis of PACG by analyzing its morphometric parameters and their association with IOP. We reviewed publications in which choroidal parameters were assessed mainly using optical coherence tomography, including measurements of choroidal thickness and calculation of the choroidal vascularity index (CVI

glaucoma.title: [Changes in retinal light sensitivity and morphometry during surgical treatment of primary glaucoma with physiotherapeutic stimulation].
glaucoma.summary: The findings indicate that comprehensive physiotherapy potentiates improvement in retinal function after surgery in patients with advanced POAG, with the effect lasting for up to 6 months.
glaucoma.abstract: UNLABELLED: Surgery for advanced stages of primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) aims to normalize intraocular pressure (IOP). A course of physiotherapy during subsequent stages of surgical treatment may have an additional beneficial effect. OBJECTIVE: The study evaluated the effect of physiotherapy in patients with glaucomatous optic neuropathy and surgically compensated IOP. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 50 patients (64 eyes) with stage II-III POAG and indications for glaucoma surgery - nonpenetrating deep sclerectomy (NPDS). IOP, mean deviation (MD), pattern standard deviation (PSD), visual field index (VFI), average retinal nerve fiber layer thickness (AvgRNFL), and ganglion cell complex (GCC) parameters were assessed before NPDS and at 1, 3, and 6 months after surgery. In the study group, 1 month after NPDS, patients received a 2-week course of adjunctive

glaucoma.title: [The effect of topical glaucoma therapy on the corneal subepithelial layer].
glaucoma.summary: In patients with glaucoma, corneal confocal microscopy findings may be informative, with particular attention warranted to the anisotropy coefficient of corneal nerve fiber orientation and the status of Langerhans cells.
glaucoma.abstract: UNLABELLED: Glaucoma is one of the most common causes of vision loss worldwide. In Russia, more than 1 million patients with glaucoma were registered in 2022, including more than 100 000 patients with newly diagnosed glaucoma. Detection of early-stage glaucoma has improved in Russia thanks to the development of high-precision diagnostic methods. OBJECTIVE: The study aimed to assess the effect of topical therapy on the structure of corneal nerve fibers and on the status of Langerhans cells using two-way analysis of variance. MATERIAL AND METHODS: The study included 102 elderly individuals (204 eyes). The observation group consisted of patients diagnosed with stage I-III primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) receiving conservative glaucoma treatment (n=73, 146 eyes), and the comparison group consisted of ophthalmologically healthy volunteers (n=29, 58 eyes). glaucoma.title: Knock-Down of Glucocorticoid Receptor Beta (GRβ) Enhances the Ocular Hypertensive Response to Dexamethasone in C57BL/6J Mice.
glaucoma.summary: Topical ocular treatment with glucocorticoids (GCs) yields an increase in intraocular pressure (IOP) in a subset (~35-40%) of the human population, known as steroid responders. If treatment is continued, this ocular hypertension (OHT) can develop into GC-induced glaucoma. …
glaucoma.abstract: Topical ocular treatment with glucocorticoids (GCs) yields an increase in intraocular pressure (IOP) in a subset (~35-40%) of the human population, known as steroid responders. If treatment is continued, this ocular hypertension (OHT) can develop into GC-induced glaucoma. In mice, the GC-mediated OHT response is modulated by the GC receptor, which exists as two major splice variants, GRα and GRβ, in the TM cell cytosol. GRα contains a GC-binding domain. Following GC binding, the GRα-GC complex enters the TM cell nucleus and transactivates genes associated with increased synthesis/export of extracellular matrix (ECM), causing OHT. GRβ has no ligand-binding domain but appears to inhibit gene transactivation by the GRα-GC complex. glaucoma.title: Metabolic and Immunometabolic Neuroprotection in Glaucoma: Mitochondrial Dysfunction, Neuroinflammation, and Emerging Therapeutic Strategies.
glaucoma.summary: Glaucoma is increasingly recognized as a multifactorial neurodegenerative optic neuropathy in which intraocular pressure (IOP) is one of several stress amplifiers rather than a sufficient etiological explanation. …
glaucoma.abstract: Glaucoma is increasingly recognized as a multifactorial neurodegenerative optic neuropathy in which intraocular pressure (IOP) is one of several stress amplifiers rather than a sufficient etiological explanation. Vascular dysregulation, mitochondrial and metabolic vulnerability, oxidative stress, excitotoxicity, glial dysregulation, and persistent neuroimmune activation can converge on retinal ganglion cell (RGC) and optic nerve injury. This broader framework is particularly relevant to normal-tension glaucoma (NTG), which represents a large proportion of primary open-angle glaucoma in Asian populations, and to patients who continue to progress despite IOP being maintained within the target range. glaucoma.title: Ocular Hypertension and Glaucoma in Graves' Orbitopathy: A Single-Center Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
glaucoma.summary: Background/Objectives: Elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) in Graves' orbitopathy (GO) is a recognized risk factor for glaucomatous optic neuropathy, but the extent to which it translates into measurable structural and functional damage remains unclear. …
glaucoma.abstract: Background/Objectives: Elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) in Graves' orbitopathy (GO) is a recognized risk factor for glaucomatous optic neuropathy, but the extent to which it translates into measurable structural and functional damage remains unclear. This study investigated structural and functional correlations in patients with GO stratified by IOP and glaucoma status. Methods: In this retrospective, cross-sectional study, 165 adult patients with GO were stratified into three groups of 55 each: normal IOP, ocular hypertension, and clinically diagnosed glaucoma. All patients underwent clinical examination, optical coherence tomography (OCT), and, where available, standard automated perimetry. Structural and functional parameters were compared across all three groups, with post-hoc pairwise testing. Multivariable logistic regression (clinical and combined models, adjusted for smoking a

glaucoma.title: The Myopic Normal Tension Glaucoma Treatment Study (MYNT-GTS): Protocol and Baseline Characteristics of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
glaucoma.summary: Background/Objectives: To describe the study protocol and baseline characteristics of participants in the Myopic Normal-Tension Glaucoma Treatment Study (MYNT-GTS), which is a randomized controlled trial evaluating the effect of intraocular pressure (IOP)-lowering treatment on glaucoma progression in eyes with myopic normal-tension glauco …
glaucoma.abstract: Background/Objectives: To describe the study protocol and baseline characteristics of participants in the Myopic Normal-Tension Glaucoma Treatment Study (MYNT-GTS), which is a randomized controlled trial evaluating the effect of intraocular pressure (IOP)-lowering treatment on glaucoma progression in eyes with myopic normal-tension glaucoma (NTG). Methods: A prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled clinical trial and baseline cross-sectional analysis. The study enrolled 473 treatment-naïve NTG eyes with myopia (spherical equivalent ≤ -1.0 diopters or axial length [AXL] > 24.0 mm) aged 20-60 years from 9 tertiary referral centers in South Korea. Participants were randomized at a 1:1 ratio into a treated group and an untreated group managed by active surveillance, and stratified by age, baseline IOP, AXL, and visual field (VF) mean deviation (MD). Treatment was initiated or intensif

glaucoma.title: Impact of Insulin Resistance on Retinal Ganglion Cell Layer Structures: Findings from the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
glaucoma.summary: Background/Objectives: Hyperinsulinaemia reflects compensatory systemic insulin resistance and may indicate early metabolic-vascular dysregulation. We investigated associations between insulin dysregulation and the retinal neuronal structure, particularly ganglion cell layer (GCL) thickness, using Korea National Health and Nutrition Exami …
glaucoma.abstract: Background/Objectives: Hyperinsulinaemia reflects compensatory systemic insulin resistance and may indicate early metabolic-vascular dysregulation. We investigated associations between insulin dysregulation and the retinal neuronal structure, particularly ganglion cell layer (GCL) thickness, using Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES) data. Methods: We analysed KNHANES's 2019-2020 participants who underwent spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) and fasting serum insulin assessment. SD-OCT-derived GCL and retinal nerve fibre layer (RNFL) thickness were compared with fasting insulin levels and insulin resistance, which was assessed using the homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance. Multivariable linear regression models were adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, hypertension, diabetes, and intraocular pressure. To account for multiple

glaucoma.title: Selective Laser Trabeculoplasty in Open-Angle Glaucoma and Ocular Hypertension: A Narrative Review of Current Evidence.
glaucoma.summary: Selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT) has emerged as a primary or adjunctive treatment choice for lowering intraocular pressure (IOP) in open-angle glaucoma (OAG) and ocular hypertension (OHT), addressing limitations of long-term topical therapy such as adherence challenges and cumulative ocular surface burden. …
glaucoma.abstract: Selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT) has emerged as a primary or adjunctive treatment choice for lowering intraocular pressure (IOP) in open-angle glaucoma (OAG) and ocular hypertension (OHT), addressing limitations of long-term topical therapy such as adherence challenges and cumulative ocular surface burden. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the mechanisms, efficacy and durability, safety, re-treatment, and predictors of response for SLT, with additional focus on treatment parameters (180° vs. 360°), emerging laser modalities (automated direct SLT/DSLT and micropulse laser trabeculoplasty/MLT), and economic and real-world effectiveness considerations. Mechanistically, SLT is based on selective photothermolysis of pigmented trabecular meshwork cells, aiming to minimize collateral structural damage and thereby support repeatability. glaucoma.title: Bovine pericardium as a patch graft in glaucoma drainage implant surgery: a case series.
glaucoma.summary: In this short-term follow-up study, bovine pericardium may be a viable alternative for coverage of glaucoma drainage implants. Larger studies with longer follow-up periods are warranted to confirm these findings.
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the short-term safety and efficacy of bovine pericardium as a patch graft in glaucoma drainage implant surgery. METHODS: We included 10 eyes from 10 patients with glaucoma. All patients underwent glaucoma drainage implant surgery using a bovine pericardial patch graft. The pericardial membrane was trimmed to 5 × 7 mm and used to cover the tube's scleral track. Intraocular pressure, best-corrected visual acuity, and the number of antiglaucoma medications were assessed preoperatively and postoperatively on Days 1, 7, 14, 28, 45, 60, 75, and 90. Conjunctival hyperemia and intraocular inflammation were clinically graded postoperatively. Symptoms, including foreign body sensation, itching, and tearing, as well as postoperative complications, were recorded. Surgical failure was defined as tube exposure resulting from erosion of the overlying patch graft and conjunctiva. RE

glaucoma.title: Trends in glaucoma diagnosis and medical management in Germany: A nationwide claims data analysis over 10 years.
glaucoma.summary: After increasing until 2019, the number of documented glaucoma patients in Germany declined despite an ageing population. Concurrently, treatment strategies shifted towards intensified medical therapy with greater use of multiple medications and fixed combinations, particularly prostaglandin-based regimens.
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: Analysing longitudinal trends in recorded diagnosis and medical management of glaucoma in Germany over a 10-year period. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study using nationwide outpatient claims and prescription data from the German statutory health insurance system. Patients with documented glaucoma or glaucoma suspect (ICD-10 H40.*) between 2014 and 2023 were included. Analyses assessed annual diagnosed glaucoma patients, demographic characteristics, proportions of medically treated patients and prescribing patterns of glaucoma medications. Trends in medication classes and number of active ingredients per patient were evaluated. RESULTS: In 2014, 2 065 065 glaucoma patients were registered. Documented patient numbers increased until 2019, reaching 2 129 673 and subsequently declined after the pandemic year to 2 025 226 in 2023. Mean patient age increased from 71.0 to 72.4 years

glaucoma.title: Real-World Multicenter Evaluation of Ab-Interno Canaloplasty Using a New Canaloplasty Device with and without Concomitant Phacoemulsification in Uncontrolled Open-Angle Glaucoma: 12-Month Outcomes.
glaucoma.summary: In real-world practice, ab-interno canaloplasty performed using iTrack Advance in mild-to-moderate uncontrolled OAG achieved significant and sustained reductions in IOP and medication burden over 12 months with a favorable safety profile.
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: To report real-world outcomes of ab-interno canaloplasty using the second-generation iTrack Advance in patients with open-angle glaucoma (OAG). PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective, observational, multicenter study reviewed consecutive ab-interno canaloplasty procedures performed using the iTrack Advance (Nova Eye Medical, US) across 11 US sites between 2022 and 2024. Eligible eyes had mild-to-moderate OAG, uncontrolled baseline intraocular pressure (IOP) ≥18 mmHg and <36 mmHg and at least 12 months of follow-up. Outcome measures included IOP and topical medication burden at 1, 6 and 12 months postop. Secondary outcomes included surgical success according to American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) criteria. Safety outcomes included complications, visual field mean deviation (VF MD), and additional glaucoma procedures. RESULTS: Eighty-two eyes of 82 patients (mean age 72.0±7.

glaucoma.title: Comparison of Surgically Induced Astigmatism After Glaucoma Filtering and Implant Procedures.
glaucoma.summary: At 3 months, LEC was associated with greater keratometric SIA than EXP, PSM, and AGV. Significant with-the-rule-oriented directional non-uniformity was detected only after LEC.
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare keratometric surgically induced astigmatism (SIA) at 3 months after trabeculectomy (LEC), EX-PRESS shunt (EXP), PRESERFLO MicroShunt (PSM), and Ahmed glaucoma valve (AGV) with ciliary-sulcus tube insertion using vector analysis, and to assess the directionality of SIA. STUDY DESIGN: Single-center, nonrandomized, retrospective comparative study. SUBJECTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 100 eyes with glaucoma undergoing LEC (n = 20), EXP (n = 30), PSM (n = 30), or AGV (n = 20) at a single center. Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), intraocular pressure (IOP), and keratometric astigmatism were evaluated preoperatively and at 3 months postoperatively. SIA was calculated using the Jaffe vector method. Directional non-uniformity of the SIA axis was assessed using the Rayleigh test after double-angle transformation. glaucoma.title: Increased incidence of glaucoma and intraocular pressure fluctuation after vitrectomy for macular hole and macular pucker.
glaucoma.summary: Higher postoperative IOPF and higher glaucoma incidence were observed in eyes that underwent vitrectomy for MP or MH.
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the incidence of glaucoma and changes in intraocular pressure fluctuation (IOPF) after vitrectomy for macular pucker (MP) and macular hole (MH). MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective cohort study, 778 patients who underwent only one vitrectomy for MP or MH were enrolled from the Chang Gung Research Database. Glaucoma development was defined as the continuous prescription of anti-glaucoma medication for more than 3 months, and the diagnosis was made later than 60 days postoperatively (index date). Postoperative IOPF was defined as the standard deviation (SD) of IOP measurements after the index date, whereas postoperative pretreatment IOPF was defined as the SD of IOP measured from the index date until the initiation of glaucoma treatment. The incidence of postoperative glaucoma and IOPF in vitrectomized eyes was compared with those in the nonvitr

glaucoma.title: The Effect of Adjunctive Mitomycin C on Outcomes of Phaco-Viscocanalostomy in Glaucoma: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
glaucoma.summary: The addition of MMC to phaco-viscocanalostomy did not provide statistically or clinically significant benefits in IOP control (clinically meaningful change defined as ≥ 2.5 mmHg IOP reduction), visual outcomes ( ≥ 0.1 logMAR change), or medication burden ( ≥ 1-medication reduction) over 6 months in patients with open-angle glaucoma. …
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate whether adjunctive intraoperative mitomycin C (MMC) improves intraocular pressure (IOP) control, visual acuity, or medication burden in patients undergoing phaco-viscocanalostomy for moderate to advanced open-angle glaucoma. METHODS: This double-masked, parallel-group randomized clinical trial included 92 eyes of 92 patients with medically uncontrolled open-angle glaucoma, who were randomly assigned to undergo phaco-viscocanalostomy with (n = 46) or without (n = 46) adjunctive MMC (0.02% for 90 seconds). Outcomes including IOP, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), cup-to-disc ratio (C/D), and number of glaucoma medications were assessed at baseline, 1 week, and 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively. RESULTS: After excluding 15 patients (9 lost to follow-up and 6 intraoperative rupture of the trabeculo-Descemet's window), 77 patients (36 in the MMC group and 41 in the co

glaucoma.title: Leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 is involved in the microtubule-mediated regulation of intraocular pressure.
glaucoma.summary: Leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) is known as the most common gene responsible for familial Parkinson disease (PD). This protein plays a key role in the neurodegenerative pathways associated with PD. LRRK2 also plays critical roles in actin dynamics and microtubule cytoskeletal assembly in the cells. …
glaucoma.abstract: Leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) is known as the most common gene responsible for familial Parkinson disease (PD). This protein plays a key role in the neurodegenerative pathways associated with PD. LRRK2 also plays critical roles in actin dynamics and microtubule cytoskeletal assembly in the cells. In addition to PD, actin and microtubule cytoskeletons are associated with the onset and development of glaucoma by regulating the intraocular pressure (IOP) in humans and animals. However, the role of LRRK2 in regulating IOP remains unclear. Hence, this study investigated the contribution of LRRK2 to cytoskeleton-mediated regulation of IOP. LRRK2 was detected in primary human trabecular meshwork cells by immunofluorescence and western blotting analysis. glaucoma.title: Therapeutic Window of AAV-SIRT1 Gene Therapy in Mouse Models of Optic Nerve Degeneration.
glaucoma.summary: SIRT1 gene therapy confers robust RGC neuroprotection and potentially preserves visual function when delivered before or after disease onset in the models of ocular hypertension and optic neuritis.
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: Optic neuropathies involve progressive loss of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and their axons, leading to irreversible vision deficits. While pretreatment with drugs or gene therapy that upregulate sirtuin 1 (SIRT1), an NAD⁺-dependent deacetylase, has shown neuroprotective effects, its effectiveness when administered after disease onset remains uncertain. We investigated whether adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated SIRT1 overexpression in RGCs can provide post-onset neuroprotection in preclinical models of optic neuropathy. METHODS: RGC degeneration was induced in C57BL/6 mice (8-10/group) using two models: elevated intraocular pressure via intracameral magnetic microbeads (glaucoma model), and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein immunization to induce optic neuritis in an experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE model). glaucoma.title: Impact of Glucagon-Like Peptide 1 (GLP-1) and Gastric Inhibitory Polypeptide (GIP) Receptor Agonists on Intraocular Pressure in Glaucoma: A Case Series.
glaucoma.summary: These cases demonstrate a potential association between GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist use and IOP lowering in patients with glaucoma and help substantiate existing literature with real world cases, thereby highlighting the need for further prospective research on this emerging topic.
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: Glucagon-Like Peptide 1 Receptor Agonists (GLP-1RAs) are antidiabetic and weight management medications that bind to GLP-1 receptors throughout the body. Growing interest in this class has led to several retrospective cohort studies reporting a decreased occurrence of glaucoma in diabetic and non-diabetic patients with the use of GLP-1RAs, suggestive of anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective effects. Here we report five real world cases evaluating the impact of GLP-1RA and dual GLP-1/Gastric Inhibitory Polypeptide (GIP) receptor agonist use on Intraocular Pressure (IOP) measurements and subsequent disease management in glaucoma patients. glaucoma.title: The Adjunctive Effect of Goniotomy Combined with Phacoemulsification and Goniosynechialysis for Advanced Primary Angle-Closure Glaucoma with 360° Angle Closure: 12-Month Outcomes.
glaucoma.summary: In advanced PACG eyes with 360° angle closure, the differences between the 12-month IOP control, surgical success, and medication reduction of the two groups showed no statistically significance. Routine addition of goniotomy may not provide additional benefit.
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare phacoemulsification with intraocular lens implantation and goniosynechialysis, with or without adjunctive goniotomy, in advanced primary angle-closure glaucoma with complete circumferential angle closure. DESIGN: Retrospective comparative study. METHODS: This study included 61 eyes undergoing phacoemulsification and goniosynechialysis without (N=31) or with adjunctive goniotomy (N=30), with at least 12 months of follow-up. A peripheral anterior synechiae of 360° was confirmed by gonioscopy and ultrasound biomicroscopy. The primary outcome was month-12 intraocular pressure (IOP). Longitudinal generalized estimating equations adjusted for baseline IOP, age, sex, and vertical cup-to-disc ratio. glaucoma.title: Topical Tacrolimus in Ocular Disease: A Narrative Review of Mechanism of Action and Therapeutic Applications.
glaucoma.summary: Topical tacrolimus is an effective steroid-sparing immunomodulator for a broad spectrum of T-cell-mediated ocular disease, with a favorable safety profile notable for the absence of steroid-related rises in intraocular pressure or cataractogenesis. Standardized formulations and prospective comparative trials remain priorities.
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: Immune-mediated inflammatory disorders of the ocular surface and anterior segment frequently require sustained immunosuppression, yet prolonged topical corticosteroid use carries the risk of glaucoma, cataract, and infection. Tacrolimus, a macrolide calcineurin inhibitor, has emerged as a steroid-sparing alternative for T-cell-mediated ocular disease. This review summarizes the mechanism of action, ocular pharmacology, clinical applications, and safety profile of topical tacrolimus. METHODS: Narrative synthesis of the peer-reviewed literature. RESULTS: Tacrolimus binds the immunophilin FK506-binding protein 12; the resulting complex inhibits the phosphatase calcineurin, preventing dephosphorylation and nuclear translocation of the nuclear factor of activated T-cells (NFAT) and thereby suppressing transcription of interleukin-2 and a broad program of pro-inflammatory cytokines. glaucoma.title: Unveiling Current Profile of Secondary Glaucoma from A Tertiary Eye Care Centre In Southern India.
glaucoma.summary: INTRODUCTION: Secondary glaucoma is a significant cause of visual morbidity and present a major challenge to ophthalmologists. Given their varied aetiological profile across regions, understanding the current spectrum is essential for early detection, timely diagnosis, and prompt management to prevent irreversible vision loss. …
glaucoma.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Secondary glaucoma is a significant cause of visual morbidity and present a major challenge to ophthalmologists. Given their varied aetiological profile across regions, understanding the current spectrum is essential for early detection, timely diagnosis, and prompt management to prevent irreversible vision loss. OBJECTIVE: To determine the clinical profile and aetiological pattern of secondary glaucoma in a tertiary eye care centre in Southern India. METHODOLOGY: This hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted at a tertiary eye care centre in Southern India from 2023 December to 2024 May. Consecutive sampling technique was utilised and ethical approval was taken. Patients diagnosed with secondary glaucoma, based on defined inclusion criteria, were enrolled after obtaining ethical approval. All patients underwent a comprehensive ophthalmic evaluation including visua

glaucoma.title: Knowledge, Willingness, and Preferences of Glaucoma Patients on Telemedicine and Vision Centres in South India.
glaucoma.summary: Glaucoma patients demonstrated moderate awareness but a positive attitude toward both telemedicine and VCs for follow-up care. Enhancing the capabilities of VCs is essential, as they are the preferred for follow-up visits and can optimise long-term glaucoma management.
glaucoma.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness, affects 80 million people globally, is projected to surpass 111 million by 2040. In India, limited availability of ophthalmologists, especially in rural areas, limits glaucoma care. Telemedicine bridges this gap by enabling remote consultations, reducing travel-related barriers and improving access to specialist services. A tertiary eye care centre in South India operates over 100 vision centres (VCs), providing primary eye care through telemedicine. However, evidence regarding glaucoma patients' acceptance remain limited, particularly in low and middle-income countries. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate glaucoma patients' knowledge, perceptions, and preferences regarding telemedicine, particularly through VCs. METHODOLOGY: This analytical, cross-sectional study included patients aged 18 years or older with stable glaucoma (well-con

glaucoma.title: Severity of Primary Open Angle Glaucoma at First Presentation and Associated Factors in Tertiary Hospital.
glaucoma.summary: Approximately half of the patients with POAG presented with severe glaucoma at diagnosis. Older age, elevated IOP, and thin CCT were key predictors of severe glaucoma at diagnosis, while patients with systemic hypertension were associated with earlier detection.
glaucoma.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Glaucoma is one of the leading causes of irreversible blindness worldwide. Late presentation in glaucoma significantly increases the economic burden and risk of subsequent blindness. OBJECTIVE: To determine the severity of glaucoma at diagnosis and identify the factors associated with severe disease at presentation in a tertiary eye hospital in Nepal. METHODOLOGY: A hospital-based, analytical, cross-sectional study was performed at Himalaya Eye Hospital from 2023 January to 2023 December among 173 eyes of 173 newly diagnosed cases of primary open angle glaucoma (POAG) after ethical clearance. Convenience sampling technique was used. The severity of glaucoma was assessed in terms of visual field (VF) loss using mean deviation (MD) and the Hoddap-Parrish-Anderson criteria. glaucoma.abstract: BACKGROUND: Blau syndrome is a rare NOD2-associated autoinflammatory disorder characterized by granulomatous arthritis, dermatitis, and uveitis. Ocular involvement may be severe in pediatric patients. Detailed reports on cataract surgery and postoperative management in children with Blau syndrome remain limited. Her articular manifestations were well controlled under systemic treatment, but she developed severe bilateral ocular involvement, including chronic uveitic changes, complicated cataracts, and vitreous opacities. glaucoma.title: Trabeculectomy versus Transscleral Cyclophotocoagulation as a Primary Surgical Procedure in Glaucoma: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
glaucoma.summary: Both procedures reduced IOP at 12 months as primary glaucoma surgeries. TRAB achieved lower final IOP, required fewer medications, and was associated with improved quality of life, whereas CPC required more adjunctive medication and retreatment in some eyes.
glaucoma.abstract: PRCIS: In this randomized multicenter trial, both TRAB and CPC lowered IOP at 12 months as primary glaucoma surgeries, with TRAB yielding lower final IOP with fewer medications, while both procedures demonstrated meaningful clinical effectiveness. PURPOSE: To compare the efficacy and safety of trabeculectomy (TRAB) and slow-burn transscleral cyclophotocoagulation (CPC) as primary surgical treatments for glaucoma. METHODS: Prospective, randomized, multicenter trial including one eye per patient from July 2020 to July 2023, with 12-month follow-up. Participants were allocated to TRAB (GI) or CPC (GII). The primary endpoint was surgical success at 12 months, defined by intraocular pressure (IOP) between 6 and 18 mm Hg without non-protocol glaucoma surgery or serious complications. glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: To report long-term postoperative outcomes of micropulse transscleral cyclophotocoagulation (MP-TSCPC) in patients with glaucoma. SUBJECTS AND METHODS: This study investigated 50 eyes in 45 patients (mean age: 67.5 ± 13.4 years) who underwent MP-TSCPC and had at least 24 months of postoperative follow-up. Causative diseases were primary open-angle glaucoma (38 eyes), pseudoexfoliation glaucoma (5 eyes), neovascular glaucoma (3 eyes), secondary glaucoma (3 eyes), and ocular hypertension (1 eye). glaucoma.abstract: Normal-tension glaucoma (NTG) is a distinct form of glaucomatous optic neuropathy characterized by progressive retinal ganglion cell (RGC) degeneration and visual field loss despite intraocular pressure (IOP) remaining within the statistically normal range. Although IOP reduction remains the only established disease-modifying strategy, continued disease progression despite adequate IOP control highlights the importance of IOP-independent mechanisms. Increasing evidence implicates vascular dysregulation, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, impaired autophagy, neuroinflammation, axonal transport abnormalities, and circadian dysregulation in increased RGC vulnerability. glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare 48-month outcomes of stent-based versus non-stent trabecular minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS) performed with phacoemulsification in open-angle glaucoma. DESIGN: Retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study. PARTICIPANTS: 250 eyes of 250 patients with open-angle glaucoma, matched 1:1 into Stent and Non-Stent groups. METHODS: All eyes underwent combined phacoemulsification and trabecular MIGS and were followed through 48 months. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was surgical success through 48 months at IOP thresholds of ≤15 mmHg and ≤18 mmHg, defined as achieving target IOP, on reduced (qualified) or without (complete) glaucoma medications and ≥20% IOP reduction from baseline without secondary incisional glaucoma surgery. glaucoma.abstract: BackgroundGlaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) arising as the most common subtype. Recent studies have shown that muscarinic and prostaglandin pathways can modulate bone remodeling under systemic, context-dependent conditions. M3 muscarinic receptor activation has been linked to increased bone formation and decreased resorption, whereas continuous prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) administration inhibits bone resorption, with intermittent use inducing bone formation. glaucoma.abstract: We report a case of distinctive ripple-like Descemet membrane folds after combined microhook ab interno trabeculotomy (µLOT) and cataract surgery. A 70-year-old Japanese man with primary open-angle glaucoma and cataract underwent nasal µLOT followed by phacoemulsification and intraocular lens implantation in the right eye. At 1 week postoperatively, unusual ripple-like Descemet membrane folds, which had not been noted at the examination on postoperative day 1, were observed in the inferior cornea with localized corneal edema. Best-corrected visual acuity was 0.4 in decimal notation. Multimodal imaging revealed no apparent Descemet membrane detachment or tears. METHODS: The medical records of children (<18 years) with glaucoma or suspected glaucoma with IOP measured by Goldmann applanation tonometry (GAT) and either pneumotonometry or rebound tonometry at a single institution from March 2018 to August 2024 were reviewed retrospectively. The difference between measurements was recorded for each eye. Correlation and Bland-Altman analysis were used to evaluate the level of agreement between tonometers. Canaloplasty is a relatively new surgical non-penetrating procedure for restoring the natural outflow pathway of aqueous humour. The aim of canaloplasty is to permanently distend the collapsed Schlemm's canal with the placement of a 360° intracanalicular tension suture. Five groups of IOP-lowering eye drops have varying mechanisms of action. Some drops, such as β-blockers and α-2 agonists, have potentially serious systemic side effects. …
glaucoma.abstract: Glaucoma is an irreversible progressive optic neuropathy, for which the major proven treatment is to lower the intraocular pressure (IOP). Five groups of IOP-lowering eye drops have varying mechanisms of action. Some drops, such as β-blockers and α-2 agonists, have potentially serious systemic side effects. Acetazolamide is the only available oral agent; it is effective at lowering IOP, but significant side effects relegate its use usually to refractory glaucoma. Two new eye drops, netarsudil and latanoprostene bunod, have recently been approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration. Both have novel IOP-lowering mechanisms and target the conventional aqueous outflow system. Selective laser trabeculoplasty is a gentle treatment that enhances conventional aqueous outflow. glaucoma.summary: Compared with medication, SLT provided a stable, drop-free IOP control to 74.2% of patients for at least 3 years, with a reduced need for surgery, lower cost and comparable HRQoL. Based on the evidence, SLT seems to be the most cost-effective first-line treatment option for OAG and OHT, also providing better clinical outcomes.

Selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT) is a safe alternative to drops and is rarely used as first-line treatment. OBJECTIVES: To compare health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in newly diagnosed, treatment-naive patients with OAG or OHT, treated with two treatment pathways: topical IOP-lowering medication from the outset (Medicine-1st) or primary SLT followed by topical medications as required (Laser-1st). glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Glaucoma management during pregnancy is a complex challenge, which requires balancing the clinical disease of the mother with the potential risks of therapy to the developing child. Because systematic studies are lacking in the pregnant population, this review aims to collect the array of available data from observational studies and case reports to provide the reader with guidance and context for the safety of glaucoma interventions during pregnancy. RECENT FINDINGS: Surgical glaucoma is a rapidly expanding field with many new technologies and procedures. We review the surgical options for the gravid patient with reference to traditional procedures like trabeculectomy and tube-shunts, and newer MIGS procedures. glaucoma.title: Evaluating glaucoma surgeries in the MIGS context.
glaucoma.summary: The challenges of glaucoma management are many: the disease is chronic, progressive, often asymptomatic, and very often, the quality of life and costs of treatment is unacceptable to the patient. This is true for both medical therapy and conventional glaucoma surgery. …
glaucoma.abstract: The challenges of glaucoma management are many: the disease is chronic, progressive, often asymptomatic, and very often, the quality of life and costs of treatment is unacceptable to the patient. This is true for both medical therapy and conventional glaucoma surgery. The choice of therapy, especially the transition from the former to the latter, is now being bridged by Minimally Invasive Glaucoma Surgeries (MIGS). Choosing from the several options now available in the surgical armamentarium requires a deeper understanding of the available modalities. This review aims to provide an overview of the decision-making process, keeping in mind age, type of glaucoma, life expectancy, socioeconomic status, patient expectations, and coexisting cataract.

glaucoma.summary: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This article examines the current literature reporting updates on trabeculectomy techniques, complications, and cost-effectiveness. RECENT FINDINGS: Trabeculectomy continues to be the standard for glaucoma surgery when a low intraocular pressure is required. …
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This article examines the current literature reporting updates on trabeculectomy techniques, complications, and cost-effectiveness. RECENT FINDINGS: Trabeculectomy continues to be the standard for glaucoma surgery when a low intraocular pressure is required. Recent publications describe technique modifications that successfully increase efficacy and lower complications. There is also an ongoing effort to define the role of trabeculectomy in the management of glaucoma from a cost and public health standpoint. SUMMARY: The current literature continues to support the use of trabeculectomy as a method of lowering intraocular pressure in glaucoma management. Efficacy has been improved by ongoing surgical innovation, and reported complication rates are lower than those previously noted. glaucoma.abstract: Laser trabeculoplasty has an increasing important role in the management of glaucoma as more emphasis is placed on minimally invasive therapies. In recent years, the following laser trabeculoplasty technologies have been introduced: micropulse laser trabeculoplasty, titanium-sapphire laser trabeculoplasty and pattern scanning trabeculoplasty. These lasers help to reduce the intraocular pressure (IOP) and the burden of glaucoma medical therapy. Literature findings regarding the safety and efficacy of these newer forms of laser trabeculoplasty in the treatment of open-angle glaucoma is summarised. These relatively newer procedures appear to have similar efficacy when compared with the former selective laser trabeculoplasty or argon laser trabeculoplasty. glaucoma.abstract: Selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT) is an effective treatment option for the reduction of intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients with ocular hypertension or open-angle glaucoma. The mechanism by which SLT lowers IOP is not completely understood and is likely multifactorial. Published studies indicate that SLT is at least as effective as argon laser trabeculoplasty or medications at lowering IOP in many forms of glaucoma. In addition to IOP reduction, SLT may decrease IOP fluctuation and can be successfully used as primary or adjunctive therapy for the management of both early and advanced glaucoma. However, SLT may not be effective in certain forms of glaucoma, and the IOP-lowering effect seems to wane with time. glaucoma.summary: We are currently in the midst of a surge in interest in glaucoma surgery. Novel pathways for reducing intraocular pressure (IOP) have been tried with various levels of success over the last few years. …
glaucoma.abstract: We are currently in the midst of a surge in interest in glaucoma surgery. Novel pathways for reducing intraocular pressure (IOP) have been tried with various levels of success over the last few years. While the trabecular bypass and suprachoroidal approaches have captured much of the attention, filtering aqueous into the sub-conjunctival space remains the gold standard for lowering IOP. This review attempts to focus on current research in surgical methods to enhance filtration by potentially improving on tried and tested methods like the trabeculectomy, deep sclerectomy, and tube surgeries.

glaucoma.title: [MINIMALLY INVASIVE GLAUCOMA SURGERIES].
glaucoma.summary: The goal of all glaucoma surgery is to lower eye pressure to prevent or reduce damage to the optic nerve. Standard glaucoma surgeries - trabeculectomy, ExPRESS shunts and external tube-shunts like the Ahmed and Baerveldt valves - are major surgeries. …
glaucoma.abstract: The goal of all glaucoma surgery is to lower eye pressure to prevent or reduce damage to the optic nerve. Standard glaucoma surgeries - trabeculectomy, ExPRESS shunts and external tube-shunts like the Ahmed and Baerveldt valves - are major surgeries. While they are very often effective at lowering eye pressure and preventing progression of glaucoma, they have a long list of potential complications. Minimal invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS) is a group of operations that have been developed in recent years to reduce some of the complications of most standard glaucoma surgeries. MIGS procedures work by using microscopic-sized equipment and tiny incisions. The purpose of this study is to review the available MIGS currently in use, their benefits and limitations.

glaucoma.abstract: Guarded external fistulization procedures remain important surgical options for patients who are experiencing progressive vision loss caused by glaucoma. The progenitor procedure, the trabeculectomy, has undergone continuous modifications over the past 40 or more years, rendering the surgery safer and the outcomes more predictable. Studies are cumulating to show that very low intraocular pressures can both reduce glaucomatous vision loss and positively change the rate of progression. Optimal patient selection and patient preparation, as well as some guiding procedural principles, are described in this review.

glaucoma.abstract: Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness in Africa. The condition is treatable but not curable. There are numerous obstacles to glaucoma care in Africa, including availability, accessibility and affordability of treatments, as well as medication nonadherence among patients. Medical therapy is costly relative to the average income in Africa and it requires daily self-dosing by patients. Surgery is of limited availability in many regions in Africa, and a high proportion of patients refuse surgery because it is expensive. Selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT) proves to be a favorable alternative to medical or surgical care, as it is highly effective and safe in people of African descent, more cost-effective than medical therapy, quick and easy to perform, and portable. The mainstay of treatment is lowering of intraocular pressure (IOP) through the use of medications, laser and/or incisional surgery. The trabecular meshwork (TM) is thought to be the site of significant resistance to aqueous outflow in open angle glaucoma. Theoretically, an incision through TM or TM removal should decrease this resistance and lead to a significant reduction in IOP. This approach, commonly referred to as goniotomy or trabeculotomy, has been validated in the pediatric population and has been associated with long-term IOP control. glaucoma.title: Mechanisms of selective laser trabeculoplasty: a review.
glaucoma.summary: Selective laser trabeculoplasty is a safe and effective treatment for glaucoma, with greater cost effectiveness than its pharmacological and surgical alternatives. glaucoma.abstract: Selective laser trabeculoplasty is a safe and effective treatment for glaucoma, with greater cost effectiveness than its pharmacological and surgical alternatives. Nevertheless, although the basic science literature on selective laser trabeculoplasty continues to grow, there remains uncertainty over the mechanism by which laser trabeculoplasty reduces intraocular pressure. To address this uncertainty, the evidence behind several potential biological and mechanical mechanisms of selective laser trabeculoplasty were reviewed. In particular, cytokine secretion, matrix metalloproteinase induction, increased cell division, repopulation of burn sites and macrophage recruitment were discussed. Refining our understanding of these mechanisms is essential both to understanding the pathophysiology of ocular hypertension and developing improved therapies to treat the condition.

glaucoma.abstract: Control of intraocular pressure (IOP) is the goal of trabeculectomy, and pursuit of this goal does not end with the completion of the surgical procedure. Proper postoperative management of the trabeculectomy patient requires an understanding of possible events that alter IOP and knowledge of the treatments to control IOP. Recent changes in surgical technique, including the use of antimetabolites, have provided new challenges in the postoperative management of trabeculectomy patients. Interventions are described to restore the flow of aqueous to the filtering bleb in the early postoperative period, to manage flat anterior chambers with both high and low intraocular pressures, to manage a failing filtering bleb, and to manage hypotony. glaucoma.abstract: A technique called optical coherence tomography (OCT) has been developed for noninvasive cross-sectional imaging in biological systems. OCT uses low-coherence interferometry to produce a two-dimensional image of optical scattering from internal tissue microstructures in a way that is analogous to ultrasonic pulse-echo imaging. OCT has longitudinal and lateral spatial resolutions of a few micrometers and can detect reflected signals as small as approximately 10(-10) of the incident optical power. Tomographic imaging is demonstrated in vitro in the peripapillary area of the retina and in the coronary artery, two clinically relevant examples that are representative of transparent and turbid media, respectively.

glaucoma.abstract: Astrocytes are specialized glial cells that outnumber neurons by over fivefold. They contiguously tile the entire central nervous system (CNS) and exert many essential complex functions in the healthy CNS. Astrocytes respond to all forms of CNS insults through a process referred to as reactive astrogliosis, which has become a pathological hallmark of CNS structural lesions. Substantial progress has been made recently in determining functions and mechanisms of reactive astrogliosis and in identifying roles of astrocytes in CNS disorders and pathologies. A vast molecular arsenal at the disposal of reactive astrocytes is being defined. Transgenic mouse models are dissecting specific aspects of reactive astrocytosis and glial scar formation in vivo. Marijuana, and delta 9-THC, also exert a wide range of other effects including analgesia, anti-inflammation, immunosuppression, anticonvulsion, alleviation of intraocular pressure in glaucoma, and attenuation of vomiting. glaucoma.title: Prostaglandins and inflammation
glaucoma.summary: Prostaglandins are lipid autacoids derived from arachidonic acid. They both sustain homeostatic functions and mediate pathogenic mechanisms, including the inflammatory response. …
glaucoma.abstract: Prostaglandins are lipid autacoids derived from arachidonic acid. They both sustain homeostatic functions and mediate pathogenic mechanisms, including the inflammatory response. They are generated from arachidonate by the action of cyclooxygenase isoenzymes, and their biosynthesis is blocked by nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs, including those selective for inhibition of cyclooxygenase-2. Despite the clinical efficacy of nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs, prostaglandins may function in both the promotion and resolution of inflammation. This review summarizes insights into the mechanisms of prostaglandin generation and the roles of individual mediators and their receptors in modulating the inflammatory response. Prostaglandin biology has potential clinical relevance for atherosclerosis, the response to vascular injury and aortic aneurysm.

retina.summary: Ang-1, sFLT-1, and sST2 are closely associated with treatment response to anti-VEGF therapy in DME patients, highlighting their roles in vascular integrity, endogenous VEGF blockade, and inflammation regulation. Both the cytokines individual levels and their ratios serve as early indicators of the success of anti-VEGF treatment in DME. …
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: Diabetic macular edema (DME) remains a significant cause of vision loss despite the widespread use of anti-VEGF therapy. Nearly half of patients experience suboptimal responses in both anatomical and functional outcomes. This study correlates molecular signatures with clinical outcomes to identify associative markers of early treatment response and optimize DME management. METHODS: Serum samples from 44 DME patients, treated with ≥3 anti-VEGF injections and 6 months follow-up, classified as responders or non-responders. Multiplex bead-based assays were used to measure cytokines related to vascular integrity, inflammatory, and adhesion molecules. Statistical analysis was performed using GraphPad. RESULTS: Responders demonstrated improvement in BCVA from 20/63 (0.5 logMAR) to 20/35 (0.25 logMAR) and CRT (443 µm to 270 µm) (p < 0.01), while non-responders worsened in both parameter

retina.title: Continuous efficacy and safety of fluocinolone acetonide implant: long-term insights in diabetic macular edema patients from a portuguese hospital.
retina.summary: The 0.19 mg FAc implant was associated with sustained anatomical and functional improvements over 36 months as part of the management of refractory DME. Long-term IOP monitoring remains essential.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To assess the efficacy and safety of the 0.19 mg intravitreal fluocinolone acetonide (FAc) implant over a 36-month period in patients with refractory diabetic macular edema (DME). METHODS: Retrospective, single-center study including patients with refractory DME treated with the FAc implant, with outcomes assessed over 36 months. The primary endpoint was the proportion of eyes with CRT ≤ 280 μm at month 36. RESULTS: Ninety-one eyes from 62 patients were included, with a mean baseline BCVA of 44.7 ± 18.1 ETDRS letters, CRT of 508.6 ± 176.2 μm, and DME duration of 3.6 ± 1.9 years. Eyes had received a median of 6 anti-VEGF injections (IQR, 3-13) and 2 corticosteroid injections (IQR, 1-3), and 23 (25.3%) were phakic. retina.summary: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a leading cause of irreversible vision loss, with neovascular AMD (nAMD) characterized by choroidal neovascularization (CNV) and subretinal fibrosis. Although anti-VEGF therapy is the current standard, frequent injections and limited efficacy necessitate alternative treatments. …
retina.abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a leading cause of irreversible vision loss, with neovascular AMD (nAMD) characterized by choroidal neovascularization (CNV) and subretinal fibrosis. Although anti-VEGF therapy is the current standard, frequent injections and limited efficacy necessitate alternative treatments. The mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway contributes to AMD by promoting oxidative stress-induced apoptosis, inflammation, and angiogenesis. We evaluated the therapeutic potential of MAPK-targeting microRNAs (miRNAs) delivered via recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV). Two rAAV2.7m8-based strategies were developed: a MAPK-miR mixture (three individually packaged miRNAs: hsa-miR-122-5p, let-7a-5p, and miR-26a-5p) and an MAPK-miR tandem (all three miRNAs in one vector under separate U6 promoters). retina.summary: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) is primarily characterized by the formation of abnormal choroidal neovascularization and can lead to substantial visual impairment. Intravitreal administration of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) agents has become the standard first-line treatment for nAMD. …
retina.abstract: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) is primarily characterized by the formation of abnormal choroidal neovascularization and can lead to substantial visual impairment. Intravitreal administration of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) agents has become the standard first-line treatment for nAMD. However, challenges remain, including the need for frequent injections, considerable treatment burden, and suboptimal responses in a subset of patients. In recent years, the emergence of high-dose anti-VEGF therapies has provided a novel strategy for extending treatment intervals and optimizing long-term disease management. To address these clinical needs, the Ophthalmology Group of China Alliance for Rare Diseases/Beijing Society of Rare Disease Clinical Care and Accessibility organized a multidisciplinary panel of experts to develop this consensus. retina.title: International consensuses and guidelines on etiology, diagnosis, and treatment of retinal vein occlusion (RVO) by the Academy of Asia-Pacific Professors of Ophthalmology (AAPPO), Asia-Pacific Vitreo-retina Society (APVRS) and Academia Retina Internationalis (ARI).
retina.summary: Retinal vein occlusion (RVO) is a prevalent potentially blinding retinal vascular disease, with secondary macular edema, retinal ischemia, and ocular neovascular complications posing substantial threats to visual function. …
retina.abstract: Retinal vein occlusion (RVO) is a prevalent potentially blinding retinal vascular disease, with secondary macular edema, retinal ischemia, and ocular neovascular complications posing substantial threats to visual function. Supported by members of the Academy of Asia-Pacific Professors of Ophthalmology (AAPPO), Asia-Pacific Vitreo-retina Society (APVRS) and Academia Retina Internationalis (ARI), a consensus and guideline is provided a comprehensive update on the etiology, diagnosis and management of RVO. An updated consensus was judged necessary following numerous recent results from epidemiology studies, evolution of advanced imaging technologies and novel pharmacotherapeutics from clinical trials, including an expanding portfolio of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) agents, drug delivery systems, and emerging evidence on relevant artificial intelligence. retina.title: Study Design for ELARA, a Phase 3b Trial of Aflibercept 8 mg in Previously Treated Patients With Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration or Diabetic Macular Edema.
retina.summary: INTRODUCTION: Aflibercept 8 mg at extended dosing intervals demonstrated functional and anatomic improvements in a large majority of patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) or diabetic macular edema (DME) in pivotal trials. …
retina.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aflibercept 8 mg at extended dosing intervals demonstrated functional and anatomic improvements in a large majority of patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) or diabetic macular edema (DME) in pivotal trials. Although a subset of patients may require frequent injections to maintain disease control, the efficacy and safety of monthly dosing with aflibercept 8 mg had not been extensively assessed. The ELARA trial evaluated the tolerability and measures of efficacy of aflibercept 8 mg every 4 weeks, as well as the feasibility of dosing interval extension following 6 monthly doses of aflibercept 8 mg, in previously treated patients with nAMD or DME. METHODS: ELARA was a multicenter, open-label, 96-week, phase 3b trial. Previously treated patients with nAMD or DME who received ≥ 3 intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor injections within 5

retina.title: Clinical exit strategy in anti-VEGF therapy for neovascular AMD: incidence of recurrence and risk factors for relapse.
retina.summary: Recurrence after anti-VEGF discontinuation is common in neovascular AMD. The presence of extrafoveal intraretinal fluid and retinal pigment epithelium tear at treatment cessation may increase the risk of relapse, highlighting the need for cautious treatment exit strategies and close post-discontinuation monitoring.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the recurrence rate of neovascular activity after discontinuation of intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) therapy in patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and to identify baseline clinical and imaging factors associated with relapse following a clinical exit strategy. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, patients with neovascular AMD who discontinued anti-VEGF therapy due to a clinical decision were identified. Treatment discontinuation was based on the absence of foveal exudation on optical coherence tomography (OCT). Baseline demographic, clinical, and OCT characteristics were analyzed. The primary outcome was disease recurrence, defined as the need for a new intravitreal anti-VEGF injection during follow-up. Multivariate regression analysis was performed to identify baseline biomarkers associated with relap

retina.title: Longer-term outcomes of intravitreal therapy for neovascular age-related macular degeneration at a peripheral centre (Palmerston North eye clinic).
retina.summary: High early cessation due to end-stage disease suggests possible late presentation, underscoring the need for earlier detection and referral. Addressing logistical barriers and supporting adherence will be increasingly important as demand for anti-VEGF therapy grows with an ageing population.
retina.abstract: AIM: The aim of this study was to evaluate long-term real-world outcomes of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy for neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) at a regional New Zealand centre, with a primary focus on treatment duration and reasons for cessation. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at Palmerston North eye clinic, including all newly diagnosed eyes with nAMD initiating anti-VEGF therapy between November 2017 and August 2023. Demographic data, visual acuity, treatment duration and documented reasons for cessation were extracted from a prospectively maintained database and validated against electronic health records. RESULTS: Among 527 eyes from 446 patients, 39.8% ceased treatment.
